note: The Pitch and The Pushback for every Platinum Rose straight-bet recommendation. Keys are GAME|Side or GAME|Total and must match digest section C.

pitch.text: The number: Friday's blend makes Detroit only a 0.4-point favorite, so +3.5 carries a 3.1-point edge and protects the key number 3. The simulator has Minnesota covering 58.1% at +3.5 (Friday snapshot, not a fresh run). Bookmaker's Thursday board had MIN +3 at +102; the consensus +3.5 is the better number.

The matchup: Minnesota is 6-0, first in SRS (8.5) and in net points (+8.5 a game), while Detroit is 4-2 at a 1.7 SRS. Kyler Murray gets a Lions secondary rated high-vulnerability with safety Kerby Joseph out, which is where Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson line up. Minnesota's only Friday designation is safety Jay Ward (questionable).

Who agrees: Sharp or Square takes MIN +3.5, and Even Money uses Minnesota as a teaser leg. Spread money is close to even (49% of money on Minnesota against 58% of bets), so there is no sharp flag on either side.

pushback.text: Detroit's path: Jared Goff at home with Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs, neither carrying a Friday designation after practicing in full Thursday. A Gibbs-led early lead turns this into a one-touchdown Lions win, and the market has priced Detroit as the better team despite the records.

Who disagrees: Action Network, BettingPros and Even Money all list Lions -3. The line moved from the Action Network open of 3 to 3.5 toward Detroit, and 51% of spread money sits on Detroit with 42% of bets, a nine-point lean that is short of a flag but points the other way.

Limits: the edge comes from an SRS baseline built on six or seven games per team; it ignores schedule strength and injuries, so the 58.1% is a rough Friday figure, not high confidence. Thursday's Bookmaker parlay 740984963 also carries Detroit's moneyline, so this single partly offsets it.
